overview: Afghanistan is a landlocked country in South and Central Asia. Its capital and largest city is Kabul. For centuries it sat on trade routes linking Persia, India and Central Asia, including the Silk Road. Afghanistan has been through decades of war since the late 1970s, and in 2021 the Taliban took control of the country. Pashto and Dari are its main languages.

geography.text: The Hindu Kush mountains run through the centre and north-east of Afghanistan, where peaks rise above 7,000 metres. The narrow Wakhan Corridor in the far north-east reaches out to a short border with China. The south and west are mostly dry plateaus and desert, and farming depends on rivers fed by melting mountain snow.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot, dry summers and very cold winters, especially in the Hindu Kush mountains.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Snow leopards, Marco Polo sheep and ibex live in the high mountains of the Wakhan Corridor.

history.text: Afghanistan sat at the crossroads of empires: Alexander the Great, the Kushans, and Persian and Mughal rulers all passed through. The modern state is usually dated to 1747, under Ahmad Shah Durrani. Afghanistan fought three wars with British India and gained full independence in 1919. A Soviet invasion in 1979 began decades of war; the Taliban ruled from 1996 to 2001 and returned to power in 2021.

events.title: Durrani Empire
events.text: Ahmad Shah Durrani founds the modern Afghan state.

events.title: Full independence
events.text: Afghanistan gains control of its foreign affairs from Britain.

events.title: Soviet invasion
events.text: Soviet troops invade, beginning a ten-year war.

events.title: US-led invasion
events.text: The Taliban government is overthrown after the 11 September attacks.

events.title: Taliban return
events.text: The Taliban take Kabul as US forces withdraw.

government.text: Since August 2021 Afghanistan has been ruled by the Taliban, who call the country the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. Their Supreme Leader holds ultimate power, and there is no elected parliament. Very few countries formally recognise the Taliban government. Girls are banned from school beyond primary level and women from most jobs.

economy.text: Afghanistan is one of the poorest countries in the world. Most people depend on farming. Foreign aid, which once paid for most of the government's budget, was cut sharply after 2021. The country has large untapped reserves of copper, lithium and other minerals.

culture.text: Afghanistan's culture draws on Persian, Central Asian and South Asian traditions. Pashto and Dari are the main languages. Kite flying, carpets and poetry, especially by the Persian poet Rumi, who was born in Balkh, are part of its heritage. The giant Buddha statues of Bamiyan were destroyed by the Taliban in 2001.

items.title: Buddhas of Bamiyan
items.text: Giant statues carved into a cliff around 1,500 years ago, destroyed in 2001.

items.title: Kite fighting
items.text: Kites with glass-coated strings battle to cut each other loose.

items.title: Afghan carpets
items.text: Hand-woven rugs known for deep red patterns.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Kabuli pulao, rice with carrots, raisins and lamb, is the national dish. Bread called naan is baked in clay ovens.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Poetry is deeply loved, and the rubab, a lute, is the national instrument.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Nowruz, the spring New Year, has long been celebrated with picnics and kite flying.

sport.text: Cricket has become Afghanistan's most popular sport, and its men's team has beaten major nations, reaching the T20 World Cup semi-finals in 2024. Buzkashi, a rough game in which horse riders fight for a goat carcass, is the traditional national sport.

items.text: Reached the T20 Cricket World Cup semi-finals.

items.title: Buzkashi
items.text: Horseback riders compete to carry a goat carcass to a goal.

items.title: Rashid Khan
items.text: One of the world's best spin bowlers.

didYouKnow: Afghanistan's traditional national sport, buzkashi, is played on horseback by riders fighting over a goat carcass.
The Persian poet Rumi was born in Balkh, in what is now Afghanistan, in 1207.

keyPeople.name: Rumi
keyPeople.text: His poems of love and faith are read all over the world.
